srt_content.tooltip: The SRT subtitle content. Each entry defines a text segment and its precise start and end times. Supports character switching with [Character] tags.

narrator_voice.tooltip: Fallback narrator voice from voice folders. Used when opt_narrator is not connected. Select 'none' for engines that support direct TTS without voice cloning, such as MOSS.

seed.tooltip: Seed for reproducible TTS generation. Same seed with same inputs will produce identical results. Set to 0 for random generation.

timing_mode.tooltip:
Determines how audio segments are aligned with SRT timings:
🔹 stretch_to_fit: Stretches/compresses audio to exactly match SRT segment durations.
🔹 pad_with_silence: Places natural audio at SRT start times, padding gaps with silence. May result in overlaps.
🔹 smart_natural: Intelligently adjusts timings within 'timing_tolerance', prioritizing natural audio and shifting subsequent segments. Applies stretch/shrink within limits if needed.
🔹 concatenate: Ignores original SRT timings, concatenates audio naturally and generates new SRT with actual timings.

opt_narrator.tooltip: Voice reference: Connect Character Voices node output OR direct audio input. Takes priority over narrator_voice dropdown when connected.

enable_audio_cache.tooltip: If enabled, generated audio segments will be cached in memory to speed up subsequent runs with identical parameters.

fade_for_StretchToFit.tooltip: Duration (in seconds) for crossfading between audio segments in 'stretch_to_fit' mode.

max_stretch_ratio.tooltip: Maximum factor to slow down audio in 'smart_natural' mode. (e.g., 2.0x means audio can be twice as long). Recommend leaving at 1.0 for natural speech preservation and silence addition.

min_stretch_ratio.tooltip: Minimum factor to speed up audio in 'smart_natural' mode. (e.g., 0.5x means audio can be half as long). min=faster speech

timing_tolerance.tooltip: Maximum allowed deviation (in seconds) for timing adjustments in 'smart_natural' mode. Higher values allow more flexibility.

batch_size.tooltip: Parallel processing workers. 0 = sequential (recommended), 2+ = streaming mode. Note: Streaming often slower than sequential mode. F5-TTS doesn't support streaming yet.

UnifiedTTSSRTNode.name: UnifiedTTSSRTNode
UnifiedTTSSRTNode.category: TTS Audio Suite/🎤 Text to Speech

TTS_engine.tooltip: TTS/VC engine configuration. Supports ChatterBox TTS Engine, CosyVoice Engine, and RVC Engine for voice conversion.

source_audio.tooltip: The original voice audio you want to convert to sound like the target voice. Accepts AUDIO input or Character Voices node output.

narrator_target.tooltip: The reference voice audio whose characteristics will be applied to the source audio. Accepts AUDIO input or Character Voices node output.

refinement_passes.tooltip: Number of conversion iterations. Each pass refines the output to sound more like the target. Recommended: Max 5 passes - more can cause distortions. Each iteration is deterministic to reduce degradation.

max_chunk_duration.tooltip: Maximum duration (in seconds) for each audio chunk. Prevents OOM on long audio. Set to 0 to disable chunking entirely. Chunks are rejoined with timing-preserving concatenation, so smart splitting is recommended for cleaner joins.

chunk_method.tooltip: Chunk split method: 'smart' cuts near silence and is recommended for cleaner boundaries, while 'fixed' cuts at exact intervals and may make joins more audible.

UnifiedVoiceChangerNode.name: UnifiedVoiceChangerNode
UnifiedVoiceChangerNode.category: TTS Audio Suite/🎤 Text to Speech

engine.tooltip: ASR-capable engine configuration (for example Qwen3-TTS Engine or Granite ASR Engine). This node auto-routes to the correct ASR adapter based on the engine type.

audio.tooltip: Audio to transcribe. Accepts AUDIO, Character Voices output, or VideoHelper audio.

language.tooltip:
Language hint for ASR.
• Auto: Let the engine handle language itself when possible
• Explicit language: Better when you know the spoken language and want more predictable results

Engine caveat:
• Qwen ASR has native Auto language detection
• Granite currently supports English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, and Japanese
• Granite + forced aligner on Auto uses a truthful heuristic for timestamps: Japanese script -> Japanese mode, otherwise the generic space-delimited aligner path

task.tooltip:
Task mode:
• transcribe: Same-language transcription
• translate: Experimental speech translation to the engine's configured ASR translation target

Important:
• Translation support varies a lot by engine and backend
• In this repo, current ASR translation paths are prompt-driven rather than fully native task APIs
• Expect uneven quality depending on language pair and model
• Translation target is configured on the engine node, not here

timestamps.tooltip:
Timing detail for the ASR timing output:
• none: Text only, no reusable timed words/segments
• word: Word-level timings for timestamp-capable ASR paths

Use word timings if you plan to feed this into the Text to SRT Builder.

Granite note: word timestamps are produced by the separate Qwen forced aligner, not natively by Granite.

chunk_size.tooltip: Chunk size in seconds. 0 = no chunking (use for short audio only).

overlap.tooltip: Overlap between chunks (seconds). Helps preserve words across chunk boundaries.

enable_asr_cache.tooltip: Cache ASR results in memory so SRT tweaks are instant. Disable if you want fresh ASR every run.

TTS_engine.tooltip: Engine configuration used to route to the correct training backend. For RVC, only the shared training-relevant settings matter here, not inference-only knobs.

training_dataset.tooltip: Prepared dataset payload from an engine-specific dataset prep node. Bad data quality will hurt you more than fancy training settings.

training_config.tooltip: Engine-specific training config. If omitted, backend defaults are used, but explicit config is better if you care about checkpoint cadence, resume behavior, or reproducibility.

continue_from.tooltip: Warm-start a new run from an existing finished model or artifacts. For RVC this is not exact resume; generator weights continue, but optimizer/discriminator state starts fresh.

output_name.tooltip: Optional exported model name override. Blank uses the dataset model name.

resume.tooltip: Exact resume from saved RVC training checkpoints for the latest compatible RVC job with the same output name, dataset, and sample rate. This only works if real G_*.pth and D_*.pth checkpoints exist.

overwrite.tooltip: Reuse the resolved output name instead of making a unique suffix. Good for deliberate replacement, bad for archival. Do not use this with resume.

srt_preset.tooltip:
Readability preset for subtitle building.
Choose a preset to seed the knobs below with recommended values, then edit them as needed.
If you change a preset-derived knob, the UI will switch to Custom automatically.

Examples:
• Broadcast: conservative timing, safe desktop readability
• Netflix-Standard: similar readability with longer max duration
• Fast speech: denser subtitles for rapid speech
• Mobile: shorter lines for smaller screens
• TTS-Ready: single-line cues that stop by meaning instead of display wrapping
• TTS-Ready (Paragraphs): same TTS-ready behavior, but tuned for longer paragraph-sized cues

srt_mode.tooltip:
How subtitle cues are grouped before final display wrapping:
• smart: rebuild cues from timed words using this node's gap, duration, CPS, and merge rules. Best default for final subtitles.
• engine_segments: keep the incoming ASR/engine segments as the base chunks, then only split later for display if needed. Use this when the source segments are already good.
• words: one timed word per cue. This is mainly for debugging alignment or inspecting bad timing data.

Use smart for almost everything.

tts_ready_mode.tooltip:
Build cues for downstream TTS instead of on-screen subtitles.
This disables multi-line display wrapping pressure, keeps each cue on one line, and prefers semantic stopping points over character-count stops.

tts_ready_paragraph_mode.tooltip:
Only used when TTS-ready is enabled.
Prefer one cue per paragraph and only split if a paragraph is genuinely too long for clean TTS playback.

heuristic_language_profile.tooltip:
Language profile for heuristic defaults.
Pick a language to seed the connector and incomplete-sentence lists.
Auto uses the ASR timing language when one is available, then falls back to English.
This is only a seed. You can still edit the text fields manually after selection.

srt_max_chars_per_line.tooltip:
Maximum characters per subtitle line.
Lower = shorter lines, more splits.
Typical values: 32 mobile, 42 desktop/broadcast.

srt_max_lines.tooltip:
Maximum lines per subtitle cue.
2 is the normal default. 3 is denser but harder to read.

srt_max_duration.tooltip:
Maximum on-screen duration for a subtitle cue in seconds.
Higher = fewer splits; too high feels laggy.

srt_min_duration.tooltip:
Minimum on-screen duration in seconds.
Higher = fewer flash cues; lower = tighter sync.

srt_min_gap.tooltip:
Pause length that forces a new subtitle cue.
Higher = more merging across short pauses.

srt_max_cps.tooltip:
Maximum reading speed in characters per second.
Lower = easier reading, more splits.
Higher = denser subtitles.

dedupe_overlaps.tooltip:
Remove overlapping duplicate phrases from bad word timing data.
Useful for alignment glitches.
Can also remove real repetitions like choruses.

dedupe_window_ms.tooltip:
Time window used to detect overlapping duplicates in milliseconds.
Higher = more aggressive dedupe.

dedupe_min_words.tooltip:
Minimum matching word count before a repeated phrase is considered a duplicate.
Higher = safer.

dedupe_overlap_ratio.tooltip:
Required timing overlap ratio before duplicate text is removed.
Higher = stricter dedupe.

punctuation_grace_chars.tooltip:
Allow a sentence-ending punctuation mark to exceed the max line length by this many chars.
Helps avoid ugly breaks right before punctuation.

min_words_per_segment.tooltip:
Merge very tiny subtitle segments into neighbors.
Higher = fewer one-word cues.

min_segment_seconds.tooltip:
Merge subtitle cues shorter than this duration.
Higher = fewer micro-cues.

merge_trailing_punct_word.tooltip:
Keep a trailing word with punctuation attached to the previous subtitle when possible.
Fixes splits like "beautiful / world."

merge_trailing_punct_max_gap.tooltip:
Maximum pause allowed when bridging that trailing punctuation word.
Higher = more aggressive bridging.

merge_leading_short_phrase.tooltip:
Merge a very short phrase into the previous cue when it follows punctuation.
Fixes splits like "I'm a / riddle."

merge_leading_short_max_words.tooltip:
Maximum word count for that short leading phrase.
Higher = more aggressive merging.

merge_leading_short_max_gap.tooltip:
Maximum pause allowed when merging a short leading phrase.
Higher = more merging across pauses.

merge_dangling_tail.tooltip:
Merge a short dangling ending into the next subtitle when it ends on a connector word.
Useful for incomplete fragments.

merge_dangling_tail_max_words.tooltip:
Maximum words allowed in that dangling ending.
Higher = more aggressive merging.

merge_dangling_tail_max_gap.tooltip:
Maximum pause allowed when merging a dangling tail.
Higher = more aggressive merging.

merge_dangling_tail_allowlist.tooltip:
Comma-separated connector words treated as dangling tails.
Example: a, the, to, of, and, I'm

merge_leading_short_no_punct.tooltip:
Merge a very short follow-up into the previous subtitle even without punctuation.
Useful for awkward mid-thought splits.

merge_leading_short_no_punct_max_words.tooltip:
Maximum words in that short follow-up.
Higher = more aggressive merging.

merge_leading_short_no_punct_max_gap.tooltip:
Maximum pause allowed when merging that follow-up.
Higher = more aggressive merging.

merge_incomplete_sentence.tooltip:
Merge short continuations when the previous subtitle clearly looks incomplete.
Useful for broken questions and sentence fragments.

merge_incomplete_max_gap.tooltip:
Maximum pause allowed when merging an incomplete sentence.
Higher = more aggressive merging.

merge_incomplete_keywords.tooltip:
Comma-separated keywords that suggest the previous subtitle is incomplete.
Example: what, why, how, where

merge_incomplete_split_next.tooltip:
If the next subtitle contains multiple sentences, split it and only merge the first sentence.
Helps keep merged subtitles readable.

merge_allow_overlong.tooltip:
Allow merges even if the final subtitle exceeds max duration.
Good for songs and slow speech. Disable for strict timing limits.

normalize_cue_end_punctuation.tooltip:
Optional subtitle-style cleanup.
When enabled, removes trailing commas, periods, semicolons, and colons at the visual end of a subtitle cue.
If a cue is cleaned this way, the next cue start is uppercased to keep the subtitle flow visually coherent.

Question marks, exclamation points, and ellipses are preserved.
This is a style transform, not grammatical truth, so it stays disabled by default.

text.tooltip:
Text to use in the subtitle cues.
Use the transcript directly, feed in cleaned text from a post-process node like ASR Punctuation / Truecase, or write plain text and let the builder estimate timings.

asr_timing_data.tooltip:
Optional ASR timing JSON.
Connect it from ✏️ ASR Transcribe or paste a saved JSON blob here.
When omitted, the builder estimates subtitle timings from the text using the SRT options.

srt_options.tooltip:
Optional subtitle-building policy.
If omitted, the builder uses the Broadcast-style defaults.

voice_device.tooltip: Optional input device name match. Leave empty to use the system default device. Device lookup is deferred until recording so ComfyUI startup does not block on PortAudio.

audio_file.tooltip:
Path to audio file or drag audio file here.

Mouse Controls:
• Left click + drag: Select audio region
• Left click on region: Highlight region (green, persistent)
• Shift + left click: Extend selection
• Alt + click region: Multi-select for deletion (orange, toggle)
• Alt + click empty: Clear all multi-selections
• CTRL + left/right click + drag: Pan waveform
• Middle mouse + drag: Pan waveform
• Right click: Clear selection
• Double click: Seek to position
• Mouse wheel: Zoom in/out
• CTRL key: Shows grab cursor for panning
• Drag amplitude labels (±0.8): Scale waveform vertically
• Drag loop markers: Move startloop/endloop points

Keyboard Shortcuts:
• Space: Play/pause
• Escape: Clear selection
• Enter: Add selected region
• Delete: Delete highlighted/selected regions (Shift+Del: clear all)
• L: Set loop from selection (Shift+L: toggle looping)
• Shift+C: Clear loop markers
• Arrow keys: Move playhead (+ Shift for 10s jumps)
• +/-: Zoom in/out
• 0: Reset zoom and amplitude scale
• Home/End: Go to start/end

Region Management:
• Click region → highlights green (single, persistent)
• Alt+click region → selects orange (multiple, toggle)
• Delete works on both green highlighted and orange selected
• Regions auto-sort chronologically
• Manual regions text box: bidirectional sync with interface

Loop Functionality:
• Select region, then press L or click 'Set Loop'
• Drag purple loop markers to adjust start/end points
• Use Shift+L or 'Loop ON/OFF' to enable/disable looping
• When looping is on, playback repeats between markers

UI Buttons:
• Upload Audio: Browse and upload audio files
• Analyze: Process audio with current settings
• Delete Region: Remove highlighted or selected regions
• Add Region: Add current selection as new region
• Clear All: Remove all regions
• Set Loop: Set loop markers from selection
• Loop ON/OFF: Toggle loop playback mode
• Clear Loop: Remove loop markers

Note: Click on the waveform to focus it for keyboard shortcuts

analysis_method.tooltip:
How to automatically detect speech segments:
• silence: Finds pauses between words/sentences (best for clear speech)
• energy: Detects volume changes (good for music or noisy audio)
• peaks: Finds sharp audio spikes (useful for percussion or effects)
• manual: Use only manual regions you define below

precision_level.tooltip:
How precise timing numbers should be in outputs:
• seconds: Rounded to seconds (1.23s) - for rough timing
• milliseconds: Precise to milliseconds (1.234s) - for most uses
• samples: Raw sample numbers (27225 smp) - for exact audio editing

visualization_points.tooltip:
Waveform detail level - how many points to draw:
• 500-1000: Smooth waveform, fast rendering
• 2000-3000: Balanced detail and performance (recommended)
• 5000-10000: Very detailed, slower but precise for fine editing

audio.tooltip:
Connect audio from another node instead of using audio_file path.
This input takes priority over the file path if connected.

options.tooltip:
Optional configuration from Audio Analyzer Options node.
If connected, uses these advanced settings for analysis.
If not connected, uses sensible default values for all analysis methods.

manual_regions.tooltip:
Define your own timing regions manually.
Format: start,end (one per line)
Example:
1.5,3.2
4.0,6.8
8.1,10.5

Bidirectional sync:
• Type/paste here → syncs to interface when you click back
• Add regions on interface → automatically updates this text
• Regions auto-sort chronologically by start time

Use when analysis_method is 'manual' or to add extra regions.

region_labels.tooltip:
Optional labels for each region (one per line).
Example:
Intro
Verse 1
Chorus

Bidirectional sync:
• Type/paste custom labels here → syncs to interface
• Interface preserves custom labels when renumbering
• Auto-generated labels (Region 1, Region 2) get renumbered
• Custom labels stay unchanged during chronological sorting

Must match the number of manual_regions lines.

export_format.tooltip:
How to format the timing_data output:
• f5tts: Simple format for F5-TTS (start,end per line)
• json: Full data with confidence, labels, metadata
• csv: Spreadsheet-compatible format for analysis

All formats respect the precision_level setting.

silence_threshold.tooltip:
How quiet audio must be to count as silence (0.001-0.1):
• 0.001-0.005: Very sensitive, catches whispers as speech
• 0.01: Default, good for most recordings
• 0.05-0.1: Less sensitive, ignores background noise
Only used when analysis_method is 'silence'

silence_min_duration.tooltip:
Shortest pause to count as a break between words (0.01-2.0 seconds):
• 0.01-0.05: Catches tiny pauses between syllables
• 0.1: Default, good for word breaks
• 0.5-2.0: Only long pauses between sentences
Only used when analysis_method is 'silence'

invert_silence_regions.tooltip:
Invert silence detection to get speech regions instead:
• False: Returns silence regions (pauses between speech)
• True: Returns speech regions (inverted silence detection)
Useful for F5-TTS editing where you want speech segments
Only used when analysis_method is 'silence'

energy_sensitivity.tooltip:
How sensitive to detect volume changes (0.0-1.0):
• 0.0-0.3: Very sensitive, detects small volume changes
• 0.5: Default, balanced detection
• 0.7-1.0: Less sensitive, only major volume changes
Only used when analysis_method is 'energy'

peak_threshold.tooltip:
Minimum amplitude threshold for detecting peaks (0.001-0.5):
• 0.001-0.01: Very sensitive, catches soft consonants and emphasis
• 0.02: Default for speech, good for normal speaking volume
• 0.05-0.1: Less sensitive, only strong emphasis or loud sounds
• 0.2-0.5: Only very loud peaks
Only used when analysis_method is 'peaks'

peak_min_distance.tooltip:
Minimum time between detected peaks in seconds (0.01-1.0):
• 0.01-0.03: Very sensitive, catches rapid syllables
• 0.05: Default for speech, good for normal speech pace
• 0.1-0.2: Less sensitive, only distinct words/emphasis
• 0.5-1.0: Only major speech events
Only used when analysis_method is 'peaks'

peak_region_size.tooltip:
Size of timing region around each peak in seconds (0.02-1.0):
• 0.02-0.05: Tight regions for precise timing
• 0.1: Default, good balance for speech editing
• 0.2-0.5: Wider regions for context around peaks
• 0.5-1.0: Very wide regions for phrase-level editing
Only used when analysis_method is 'peaks'

group_regions_threshold.tooltip:
Group nearby detected regions into larger segments (0.000-3.000 seconds):
• 0.000: No grouping, keep all regions separate
• 0.001-0.050: Group very tiny gaps (remove micro-silences)
• 0.100-0.200: Group small gaps (syllables → words)
• 0.300-0.500: Group moderate gaps (words → phrases)
• 1.000-3.000: Group large gaps (phrases → sentences)
Applies to all detection methods after initial analysis

original_text.default: Some call me nature, others call me mother nature.
original_text.tooltip: Original text that matches the original audio

target_text.default: Some call me optimist, others call me realist.

edit_regions.tooltip: Edit regions as 'start,end' in seconds (one per line). These are the time regions to replace.

device.tooltip: Device to run F5-TTS model on. 'auto' selects best available (GPU if available, otherwise CPU).

model.tooltip: F5-TTS model variant to use. F5TTS_Base is the standard model, F5TTS_v1_Base is improved version, E2TTS_Base is enhanced variant.

seed.tooltip: Seed for reproducible F5-TTS generation. Same seed with same inputs will produce identical results. Set to 0 for random generation.

fix_durations.tooltip: Fixed durations for each edit region in seconds (one per line). Leave empty to use original durations.

temperature.tooltip: Controls randomness in F5-TTS generation. Higher values = more creative/varied speech, lower values = more consistent/predictable speech.

nfe_step.tooltip: Neural Function Evaluation steps for F5-TTS inference. Higher values = better quality but slower generation. 32 is a good balance. Values above 71 may cause ODE solver issues.

cfg_strength.tooltip: Speech generation control. Lower values (1.0-1.5) = more natural, conversational delivery. Higher values (3.0-5.0) = crisper, more articulated speech with stronger emphasis. Default 2.0 balances naturalness and clarity.

sway_sampling_coef.tooltip: Sway sampling coefficient for F5-TTS inference. Controls the sampling behavior during generation. Negative values typically work better.

ode_method.tooltip: ODE solver method for F5-TTS inference. 'euler' is faster and typically sufficient, 'midpoint' may provide higher quality but slower generation.

crossfade_duration_ms.tooltip: Crossfade duration in milliseconds for smooth transitions between segments

crossfade_curve.tooltip: Crossfade curve type: linear (constant), cosine (smooth), exponential (sharp)

adaptive_crossfade.tooltip: Automatically adjust crossfade duration based on segment size

enable_cache.tooltip: Cache F5-TTS generation to speed up subsequent runs with identical parameters

cache_size_limit.tooltip: Maximum number of cached audio segments to store in memory

boundary_volume_matching.tooltip: EXPERIMENTAL: Automatically match volume levels at segment boundaries to reduce clicks/pops

full_segment_normalization.tooltip: EXPERIMENTAL: Normalize entire generated segments to match surrounding original audio RMS levels

spectral_matching.tooltip: EXPERIMENTAL: Apply EQ to match spectral characteristics of original audio

noise_floor_matching.tooltip: EXPERIMENTAL: Add subtle noise to match the background noise level of original audio

dynamic_range_compression.tooltip: EXPERIMENTAL: Apply gentle compression to reduce volume spikes and make transitions smoother

post_rms_normalization.tooltip: Post-processing RMS normalization level. Applied after F5-TTS generation to normalize generated segments volume (does not affect original segments).

force_cache_clear.tooltip: Force clear cache for debugging (will regenerate F5-TTS audio)

input_audio.tooltip: Input audio to edit (0.5-30 seconds limit)

audio_text.tooltip:
Transcript of the input audio.

For paralinguistic mode: Include tags where you want sounds inserted.
Example: 'Hello <Laughter> how are you?'

Available tags: <Breathing>, <Confirmation-en>, <Dissatisfaction-hnn>, <Laughter>, <Question-ei>, <Sigh>, <Surprise-ah>, <Surprise-oh>, <Surprise-wa>, <Uhm>

edit_type.tooltip:
Type of edit to apply:
- emotion: Change emotional expression
- style: Change speaking style
- speed: Adjust speaking speed
- paralinguistic: Add non-verbal sounds (use <tags> in audio_text)
- denoise: Remove background noise
- vad: Remove silent portions

emotion.tooltip: Emotion to apply (only used when edit_type='emotion')

style.tooltip: Speaking style to apply (only used when edit_type='style')

speed.tooltip: Speed adjustment (only used when edit_type='speed')

n_edit_iterations.tooltip:
Number of editing iterations. Higher values = stronger effect but may reduce quality. 1-2 recommended for subtle changes, 3-5 for dramatic changes.

Iterations are cached - try 3, then 2, then 1 without re-running!

tts_engine.tooltip: Step Audio EditX engine configuration. If not provided, will create default engine.

StepAudioEditXAudioEditorNode.name: StepAudioEditXAudioEditorNode
StepAudioEditXAudioEditorNode.category: TTS Audio Suite/🎨 Step Audio EditX

pitch.tooltip: Pitch shift in semitones. 0=no change, +12=octave up (male→female), -12=octave down (female→male)

index_ratio.tooltip: Index file influence (0.0-1.0). Higher=more like training voice, lower=more like input voice

consonant_protection.tooltip: Consonant protection - Protects speech clarity. Low=voice changes more, High=keeps original pronunciation clearer

volume_envelope.tooltip: Volume envelope mixing - Controls volume patterns. Low=use target voice volume, High=keep original voice volume patterns

hubert_model: auto: Automatically select best available model

hubert_model.default: auto: Automatically select best available model
hubert_model.tooltip:
HuBERT Model for feature extraction:

• Auto: Automatically select the best available model based on your language
• Content Vec 768: RECOMMENDED - Best for RVC voice conversion, fastest loading
• HuBERT Japanese: Optimized for Japanese voices and phonetics  
• HuBERT Korean: Specialized for Korean speech patterns
• Chinese HuBERT: Fine-tuned for Mandarin Chinese tonal patterns
• HuBERT Large: Highest quality but slower processing

Models will auto-download if not present. Choose language-specific models for best results.

rvc_pitch_options.tooltip: Optional advanced pitch extraction settings from RVC Pitch Options node. Overrides basic parameters.

output_sample_rate.tooltip: Output sample rate (0=use input rate). 44100/48000 recommended for high quality

enable_custom_chunking.tooltip: Enable the Voice Changer's outer chunking on top of native RVC segmentation. Leave off unless you specifically need shorter-than-native chunks for extra VRAM safety. Native RVC long-audio segmentation usually starts around 64s on the common half-precision path, and lower on some fp32/low-VRAM paths.

device.tooltip:
Processing device:
• auto: Automatically select best available (MPS on Apple Silicon, CUDA on NVIDIA, XPU on Intel, CPU fallback)
• cuda: NVIDIA GPU (requires CUDA-capable GPU)
• xpu: Intel GPU (requires Intel PyTorch XPU)
• cpu: CPU-only processing (slower)
• mps: Apple Metal Performance Shaders (Apple Silicon Macs only)

RVCEngineNode.name: RVCEngineNode
RVCEngineNode.description:
RVC Engine - Real-time Voice Conversion
    
    ⚠️ Voice conversion only - does NOT generate speech from text.
    Will not work with TTS Text or TTS SRT nodes. Use with Voice Changer node only.
    
    Consolidates RVC model loading and voice conversion parameters into unified interface.
    Supports pitch shifting, advanced quality controls, and multiple pitch extraction algorithms.
    
    Key Features:
    • Voice conversion with pitch control
    • Multiple pitch extraction algorithms (RMVPE, Crepe, etc.)
    • Quality controls (index rate, consonant protection)
    • Automatic model management and caching
    • Compatible with unified Voice Changer node

pitch_detection.tooltip:
Pitch extraction algorithm:
• RMVPE: Best balance of quality & speed (recommended)
• RMVPE+: Enhanced RMVPE with better accuracy
• Mangio-Crepe: Optimized Crepe, faster than standard
• Crepe: Highest quality but slower processing
• PM: Fast Praat-based extraction, basic quality
• Harvest: Traditional method, good for speech
• DIO: Fast algorithm, lower quality
• FCPE: Very fast extraction for real-time use

crepe_hop_length.tooltip: Only used by Crepe and Mangio-Crepe methods. Lower values track pitch changes more closely but cost more time and memory.

filter_radius.tooltip: Only meaningful for Harvest smoothing in this backend. 0 means no extra smoothing; higher values smooth more but can flatten detail.

f0_autotune.tooltip: Snap the extracted pitch contour toward the nearest musical note after pitch detection. Can help singing or stylized output, but often sounds artificial on normal speech.

use_cache.tooltip: Reuse cached loaded RVC/HuBERT models where possible for repeated processing. Usually worth leaving on.

batch_size.tooltip: Crepe-family pitch batch size hint. Higher can be faster but uses more memory. Ignored by non-Crepe methods.

RVCPitchOptionsNode.name: RVCPitchOptionsNode
RVCPitchOptionsNode.description:
RVC Pitch Extraction Options - Advanced pitch control for RVC voice conversion
    
    Provides detailed configuration of pitch extraction algorithms and advanced processing options.
    Connect to RVC Engine node for enhanced voice conversion control.
    
    Voice conversion quality parameters (index_rate, protect, rms_mix_rate) are configured in the RVC Engine node.
    
    Key Features:
    • Multiple pitch extraction algorithms (RMVPE, Crepe, PM, Harvest, etc.)
    • Advanced processing options (filtering, autotune, cache, batching)
    • Performance optimization (caching, batch processing, resampling)
    • Method-specific parameters (Crepe hop length, etc.)
    
    Pitch Methods Guide:
    • RMVPE: Best overall balance of quality and speed (recommended)
    • Crepe/Mangio-Crepe: Highest quality, slower processing
    • PM: Fastest, good for real-time applications
    • Harvest: Traditional algorithm, good for speech
    • DIO/FCPE: Alternative methods for specific use cases

audio.tooltip: Input audio for restoration. Accepts ComfyUI AUDIO format (waveform + sample rate).

restoration_mode.tooltip:
🤐 VOICE FIXER RESTORATION MODES

MODE 0 - ORIGINAL (Recommended for most audio):
• Removes noise, reverberation, clipping artifacts
• Balanced approach for general degraded speech
• Works well with speech that has some background noise
• Best for: Podcasts, recordings, voice calls

MODE 1 - WITH HIGH-FREQUENCY REMOVAL:
• Original restoration + aggressive high-frequency filtering
• Removes harsh sibilants and high-frequency artifacts
• Good for audio with excessive brightness or hiss
• Best for: Overly bright recordings, high-pitched noise

MODE 2 - TRAIN MODE (Seriously Degraded):
• Uses model in training mode for maximum restoration
• Most aggressive but may introduce artifacts
• Best for severely damaged audio quality
• Warning: Can distort very clean audio
• Best for: Heavily degraded, severely clipped, or very noisy audio

💡 START WITH MODE 0 - if unsatisfactory, try MODE 1 or 2

use_cuda.tooltip: Enable CUDA GPU acceleration. Falls back to CPU automatically if not available.

TTS_engine.tooltip: Connect the RVC engine here because dataset prep also needs HuBERT and pitch-extraction settings, not just the later training node.

model_name.tooltip: Base name for the trained RVC voice. Changing only this should not force dataset re-prep when the actual data/settings stay the same.

dataset_source.tooltip: Optional folder, zip, or single audio file path. Relative paths resolve from ComfyUI input/ and input/datasets/. Clean single-speaker speech matters more than having one huge raw recording. Leave empty if you only use opt_audio inputs.

training_sample_rate.tooltip: Target training sample rate. 40k is the normal speech default and usually the right place to start.

cpu_workers.tooltip: CPU workers for slicing and feature extraction. 1-4 is usually enough; more is not automatically better, especially on Windows.

chunk_seconds.tooltip: Target clip length after slicing. RVC usually likes short clips; 3.0s is a good default, and an effective range around 2-8s is normal.

overlap_seconds.tooltip: Small overlap helps avoid harsh cuts between slices. Too much overlap just duplicates data and slows prep.

max_volume.tooltip: Peak normalization ceiling for extracted clips. 0.95 is a safe default; avoid pushing everything to 1.0 unless you like clipping risk.

mute_ratio.tooltip: Extra silence augmentation ratio. Leave this at 0 for normal training; raise it only if the model is over-voicing silence or breathing badly.

reuse_existing.tooltip: Reuse the prepared dataset cache when settings match. Usually keep this on; rebuilding features every run is just wasted time.

opt_audio1.tooltip: Optional training audio clip. Connect one or more AUDIO sources here for quick in-graph tests, or combine them with a dataset path.

epochs.tooltip: Actual RVC epoch count. Around 20 is a smoke test, 50-100 is a first real pass, and 100+ is where cleaner datasets usually become worth judging. Loss helps spot trends, but listening tests still decide quality.

batch_size.tooltip: Use the largest stable batch that fits VRAM. Bigger is usually faster and a bit smoother; lower it first if you hit OOM or instability.

learning_rate.tooltip: 1e-4 is the normal safe default. Lower it if training gets spiky or noisy; raising it is one of the fastest ways to make adversarial training worse.

gpu_ids.tooltip: CUDA device ids in the odd RVC format, for example '0' or '0-1'. Leave blank unless you deliberately want multi-GPU behavior.

num_workers.tooltip: PyTorch dataloader workers. Keep this at 0 on Windows; worker processes there can respawn ComfyUI internals and break training.

fp16_run.tooltip: Keep this on for normal CUDA training. Turn it off only if you see NaNs, weird instability, or hardware/driver-specific fp16 issues.

save_every_epoch.tooltip: Checkpoint cadence. Save a resumable training checkpoint every N epochs. 5 is a good default, 1 is safest, and 0 disables periodic resume checkpoints entirely.

cache_data_in_gpu.tooltip: Cache batches in VRAM for speed. Usually worth it if you have room; turn it off if VRAM pressure becomes the real bottleneck.

max_checkpoints.tooltip: Checkpoint retention policy. Keep the newest N checkpoint pairs and delete older ones. 1 means keep only the latest resumable checkpoint, 3 means keep the latest three, and so on.

save_every_weights.tooltip: Export extra standalone weight files at each save interval. Mostly useful for inspection or experiments; normal training does not need this.

train_index.tooltip: Build the matched FAISS index after training. Usually keep this on; normal RVC inference often sounds worse without the proper index.

save_best_model.tooltip: Track generator loss and save the lowest-loss model as an extra inference checkpoint candidate. Useful for listening tests, but lowest loss is not guaranteed to be the best sounding model.

best_model_threshold.tooltip: Initial gate for first 'best model' capture. Leave this alone unless you are debugging why low-loss checkpoint saving triggers too early or too often.

log_every_epoch.tooltip: Logging cadence within an epoch. This affects dashboard/log granularity, not training quality. 1.0 is about once per epoch, 0.5 is about twice.

pretrained_generator.tooltip: Generator initialization checkpoint. Keep this on auto unless you know exactly why you want a different base; training from scratch on a small dataset is usually a bad idea.

pretrained_discriminator.tooltip: Discriminator initialization checkpoint. Auto is the sane default and should stay matched to the generator/sample-rate setup.

c_adv.tooltip: Adversarial loss weight. Advanced knob. Do not touch this unless you are intentionally rebalancing training and understand the side effects.

c_mel.tooltip: Mel reconstruction weight. One of the main terms keeping speech recognizable. Usually leave it at default unless you are doing real loss tuning.

c_kl.tooltip: KL regularization weight. Changing this can absolutely destabilize training, so leave it alone unless you know the tradeoff you want.

c_fm.tooltip: Feature-matching weight. Usually helps texture/stability. Leave it at default unless you are deliberately rebalancing losses.

c_tefs.tooltip: Experimental TEFS auxiliary loss. Keep this at 0 unless you are explicitly experimenting with that feature.

c_hd.tooltip: Experimental harmonic-detail auxiliary loss. Keep this at 0 for normal training.

c_tsi.tooltip: Experimental TSI auxiliary loss. Keep this at 0 unless you are intentionally testing it.

c_gp.tooltip: Gradient-penalty weight. This is mostly a stabilization/debug knob, not a normal training control. Leave it at 0 unless adversarial loss is misbehaving.

use_multiscale.tooltip: Use experimental multiscale mel loss. Heavier and not needed for a normal first pass.

use_balancer.tooltip: Enable dynamic loss balancing. Advanced only. If you do not already know why you want this, you do not want this.

use_pareto.tooltip: Pareto-style balancing on top of the dynamic balancer. Ignore this unless you are already deliberately using the balancer.

fast_mode.tooltip: Speed tweak for the advanced balancer path. It does nothing useful unless you already enabled those advanced balancing options.

TTS_engine.tooltip: Connect a MOSS engine here. The first training slice only supports Delay 8B LoRA training.

model_name.tooltip: Base name for the trained MOSS LoRA adapter folder.

dataset_source.tooltip:
Path to the main MOSS manifest JSONL.
This is your training set manifest: one JSON row per clip.
In the normal workflow, connect the manifest path produced by MOSS Dataset Rows here.

validation_source.tooltip:
Optional second manifest JSONL used only for validation.

Use this if you already prepared a separate holdout set.
Example:
• dataset_source = your main training manifest
• validation_source = a smaller separate manifest reserved for evaluation

If you leave this blank, the node will automatically split dataset_source into train + validation for you.

validation_split.tooltip:
Only used when validation_source is blank.
Example: 0.05 means keep about 5% of dataset_source for validation and use the rest for training.

split_seed.tooltip: Seed for the automatic train/validation split, so the same manifest gets split the same way every time.

prep_batch_size.tooltip: Batch size for audio-code extraction during dataset prep.

n_vq.tooltip: Optional codec codebook count override. 0 uses the model default.

encode_reference_audio.tooltip:
Pre-encode reference audio fields during dataset prep.
Leave this on if your manifest uses ref_audio/reference_audio.
If you are doing normal audio+transcript training with no reference clips, this setting does not matter much.

reuse_existing.tooltip: Reuse a matching prepared dataset cache instead of re-encoding audio codes every run.

training_mode.tooltip: First MOSS training slice. This currently trains LoRA adapters for the Delay 8B base model only.

epochs.tooltip: Epoch count used when max_train_steps is 0.

max_train_steps.tooltip: Hard training-step cap. Set 0 to use epochs instead.

batch_size.tooltip: Per-device batch size. Keep it low on 8B models.

gradient_accumulation_steps.tooltip: Micro-batch accumulation. This is how you fake a larger effective batch without immediately OOMing.

learning_rate.tooltip: LoRA learning rate. The upstream Norwegian example used 2e-6.

warmup_steps.tooltip: Warmup step count before cosine decay.

max_grad_norm.tooltip: Gradient clipping. The upstream Norwegian example used 0.5.

num_workers.tooltip: Dataloader workers. 0 is the safest default.

gradient_checkpointing.tooltip: Keep this on for 8B training unless you deliberately want higher VRAM usage.

base_quantization.tooltip: Base-model VRAM strategy. 4bit_nf4 enables QLoRA-style loading of the frozen 8B base model with bitsandbytes. This is the main knob if 24 GB VRAM is still not enough.

bnb_4bit_compute_dtype.tooltip: Compute dtype used by 4-bit quantized layers. auto follows the mixed-precision choice. fp32 is safer but costs more VRAM.

bnb_4bit_use_double_quant.tooltip: Enable nested quantization for 4-bit base loading. Usually worth keeping on.

save_steps.tooltip: Checkpoint save cadence. 0 disables intermediate checkpoints.

trainable_lora_modules.tooltip: Which Delay backbone modules receive LoRA adapters. mlp matches the released Norwegian example best.

dataset_name.tooltip: Base name for the staged clip set.

output_subdir.tooltip: Subdirectory inside ComfyUI input/ where staged MOSS training clips will be written.

overwrite.tooltip: Overwrite the existing staged clip folder if it already exists.

opt_audio1.tooltip: Optional training audio clip. Connect one or more AUDIO sources here.

clip_dataset.tooltip: Staged clip dataset from MOSS Clip Staging.

manifest_name.tooltip: Output manifest filename. .jsonl will be appended if missing.

text_lines.default:
Hello there, this is a training sample.
How are you today?
text_lines.tooltip:
Exactly one line per staged clip, in clip order.
Each line is the transcription/text for that clip's target audio.
Simple training: just give each clip its own transcript here.
Example: clip001 audio says 'Hello there' -> line 1 should be 'Hello there'.

reference_clip_lines.tooltip:
Optional one line per staged clip.
Most single-speaker or fixed-voice LoRAs should leave this blank.
Use this only if a training row should also include reference audio for voice/style conditioning.
That means: text says what to say, target clip is the correct output, and reference clip says whose voice/style to follow.
Leave blank for normal audio+transcript training.
Each line may be blank, a single clip id like clip001, a 1-based clip number like 1, or a comma-separated list such as clip001,clip002.
Example: line 2 = clip001 means clip002 trains as: text from line 2 + reference voice from clip001 -> target audio clip002.
Single reference -> ref_audio. Multiple references -> reference_audio.

language_lines.tooltip: Optional one line per clip. Blank line uses default_language or no language field.

instruction_lines.tooltip:
Optional one line per clip. Blank line uses default_instruction.
Use this for explicit labels such as 'speaking angrily', 'whispering', or 'calm narration'.
Do not use this for recording/presentation labels like 'telephone call quality'; those belong in quality_lines.
For many style-focused datasets, this is easier and clearer than using reference_clip_lines.

quality_lines.tooltip:
Optional one line per clip. Blank line uses default_quality.
Use this for recording/presentation labels such as 'telephone call quality', 'studio recording', or similar audio-quality descriptors.

sound_event_lines.tooltip: Optional one line per clip. Blank line uses default_sound_event.

ambient_sound_lines.tooltip: Optional one line per clip. Blank line uses default_ambient_sound.

duration_tokens_lines.tooltip: Optional one line per clip. Blank line uses default_duration_tokens.

default_language.tooltip: Optional shared language fallback for rows whose language_lines entry is blank.

default_instruction.tooltip:
Optional shared instruction fallback for rows whose instruction_lines entry is blank.
Useful if most rows should carry the same style label, for example 'speaking angrily'.

default_quality.tooltip:
Optional shared quality fallback.
Useful if most rows share the same recording/presentation quality label, for example 'telephone call quality'.

default_duration_tokens.tooltip: Optional shared tokens fallback. 0 disables it.

output_subdir.tooltip: Subdirectory inside ComfyUI input/ where the generated manifest file will be written.

overwrite.tooltip: Overwrite the existing manifest file if it already exists.

text.default:
Enter your text here. Examples:
Polish: Cześć, jak się masz?
German: Schöne Grüße aus München!
French: Bonjour, comment allez-vous?
text.tooltip:
Input text to normalize for TTS processing.

Supports multilingual text with special characters like:
• Polish: ą, ć, ę, ł, ń, ó, ś, ź, ż
• German: ä, ö, ü, ß
• French: à, é, ê, ç, etc.
• And many other languages

Connect this to any TTS engine for improved pronunciation.

method.tooltip:
Text processing method to apply:

• Pass-through: No processing (original text)
• Unicode Decomposition: ą→a̧, ć→ć (recommended for most cases)
• IPA Phonemization: Full phonetic conversion (ą→ɔ̃, requires espeak)
• Character Mapping: ASCII fallback (ą→a, ć→c)

Start with Unicode Decomposition - it fixes most pronunciation issues.

language.tooltip:
Language for processing (affects IPA Phonemization):

• Auto-detect: Automatically detects language from text
• Manual selection: Choose specific language for better accuracy

Language detection looks for special characters:
• Polish: ą, ę, ć, ł, etc.
• German: ä, ö, ü, ß
• French: à, é, ê, ç, etc.

Only affects IPA Phonemization method.

show_debug.tooltip:
Show debug information in console:

• Original vs normalized text comparison
• Character-by-character changes
• Detected language (when auto-detecting)
• Processing method used

Helpful for testing which method works best for your language.
Disable for cleaner console output in production.

text.default: this was designed mainly for raw asr outputs like granite but it can clean up any plain text transcript as well
text.tooltip:
Raw text to post-process with punctuation and true-casing.

Designed mainly for low-punctuation ASR outputs such as Granite transcripts, but it can be used on any plain text transcript.

Important: this expects plain transcript text, not full SRT files with cue numbers and timestamps.

Best results usually come from lowercased, lightly cleaned ASR text rather than already-punctuated prose.
If a paragraph already looks properly punctuated, the node now skips repunctuating that paragraph automatically instead of making it worse.

model.tooltip:
Choose the punctuation/truecase model.

English is the lightest option.
Romance covers ES/FR/IT/PT/CA/GL.
XLM-R is the heavy multilingual fallback.

These are helper models, not ASR engines.

processing_scope.tooltip:
How to feed text to the punctuation model.

Whole Text: process the entire input as one block.
Per Paragraph: split on blank lines first and preserve paragraph breaks.

output_mode.tooltip:
How to format the output text.

Restored Paragraphs: normal punctuated text.
One Sentence Per Line: useful for subtitle prep, manual review, or later segmentation.

lowercase_input_first.tooltip:
Lowercase the input before running the punctuation model.

Recommended for raw ASR text because these helper models are mainly trained for lowercased, unpunctuated transcripts.
Disable only if you are intentionally experimenting with already-cased input.

signal.tooltip: Primary signal input. Connect this to the output of a node that creates new voice files (e.g., Voice Designer) to ensure voices are refreshed after file creation.

signal2.tooltip: Secondary passthrough signal. Use this to chain execution order: connect your ENGINE/config here, and connect signal2_out to downstream TTS nodes. This ensures TTS nodes run after voice cache refresh.

force_refresh.tooltip: Force a full rescan of voice folders and alias map.

provider.tooltip:
Computer vision provider for mouth movement detection:

• MediaPipe: Google's ML framework (preferred, incompatible with Python 3.13)
  - Fast, accurate, works on most hardware
  - Best for general use and consistent results

• OpenSeeFace: Real-time face tracking (experimental, Python 3.13 compatible)
  - Alternative for newer Python versions
  - Results may be less accurate than MediaPipe

• dlib: Traditional computer vision (coming soon)
  - Lightweight, no ML dependencies

sensitivity.tooltip:
Ultra-fine movement detection sensitivity (exponential scaling):

• 0.05-0.2: Only obvious mouth movements (conservative)
• 0.3-0.4: Clear speech detection (balanced)
• 0.5-0.6: Most speech including soft talking
• 0.7-0.8: Sensitive, catches subtle movements
• 0.9-1.0: Ultra-sensitive, includes whispers and micro-movements

Exponential scaling provides fine control at higher values.
Start with 0.5, then fine-tune in 0.01 increments.

min_duration.tooltip:
Minimum duration for valid speech segments (in seconds):

Lower values: Include quick sounds and short words, more segments
Higher values: Only longer phrases, cleaner but may miss short words

Recommended: 0.1s for balanced filtering, 0.05s for detailed analysis

output_format.tooltip:
Output format for timing data:

• SRT: Standard subtitle format, best for TTS synchronization
• JSON: Detailed data with confidence scores for analysis
• CSV: Spreadsheet format for data processing
• AUDIO_REGIONS: start,end format compatible with Audio Analyzer

Recommended: SRT for TTS workflows, AUDIO_REGIONS for audio analysis

srt_placeholder_format.tooltip:
SRT placeholder format - adapts to viseme detection:

🔌 WITHOUT Viseme Options:
• Words: [word word word] - estimated word placeholders
• Syllables: [syl-la-ble syl-la-ble] - estimated syllable patterns
• Characters: [••••••••••••••••••••] - character count

🔗 WITH Viseme Options connected:
• Words: [A EI OU] - vowels grouped as words
• Syllables: [AE-I-OU] - vowels grouped as syllables
• Characters: [AEIOU] - raw vowel sequence

Format = presentation style, visemes = actual vowel content!

viseme_options.tooltip:
Connect Viseme Mouth Shape Options node for vowel detection (A, E, I, O, U):

• When connected: Enables precise vowel classification
• When not connected: Basic speech/no-speech detection only

Viseme detection adds ~20% processing time but provides detailed mouth shape analysis for lip-sync.

preview_mode.label: Show preview with movement markers
preview_mode.tooltip:
Generate annotated video preview with movement markers:

Shows green/red overlays for detected/undetected movements with confidence scores and facial landmarks.

Performance: Uses 540p resolution, increases processing time by ~40%

Use for: Debugging detection accuracy and tuning parameters

clean_subtitle_output.label: Clean Subtitle Output
clean_subtitle_output.tooltip:
Remove all brackets, confidence scores, and metadata from output:

• OFF: [hello world] (confidence: 74.2%, 1.1s)
• ON: hello world

Use when you want clean subtitles ready for direct use without technical information.

merge_threshold.label: Merge gaps shorter than (seconds)
merge_threshold.tooltip:
Merge nearby speech segments separated by short gaps:

Lower values: Keep more segments separate, preserve natural pauses
Higher values: Merge more segments together, smoother but less detailed

Recommended: 0.2s for natural flow, 1.0s+ for sentence-level segments

confidence_threshold.tooltip:
Minimum confidence score for including detected movements:

• 0.0-0.2: Include all detections (may include noise)
• 0.3-0.4: Balanced filtering (recommended start)
• 0.5-0.7: Conservative, only clear movements
• 0.8-1.0: Ultra-strict, only highest confidence

Confidence based on landmark quality, face visibility, lighting.
With new exponential sensitivity, lower values work better.

enable_viseme_detection.label: Enable Viseme Detection
enable_viseme_detection.tooltip:
Enable vowel classification (A, E, I, O, U) for precise lip-sync:

• Analyzes mouth shape geometry beyond simple open/close
• Detects vowel patterns in mouth movements
• Adds ~20% processing time
• Provides phoneme sequences for better TTS synchronization

viseme_sensitivity.tooltip:
How hard should I look for vowels?

Controls geometric thresholds for mouth shape classification:

• 0.1-0.5: Very strict, only obvious vowel shapes
• 0.8-1.2: Balanced detection (recommended)
• 1.5-2.0: Lenient, detects subtle vowel variations

Higher = more detections, may include false positives
Lower = fewer detections, higher accuracy

viseme_confidence_threshold.tooltip:
How sure should I be before showing a vowel?

Minimum confidence for valid viseme classification:

• 0.0-0.2: Show all viseme attempts (noisy)
• 0.3-0.5: Balanced filtering (recommended)
• 0.6-0.8: Conservative, only clear vowels
• 0.9-1.0: Ultra-strict, only perfect detections

Below threshold shows as 'neutral' instead of uncertain vowel.

viseme_smoothing.tooltip:
Temporal smoothing to reduce viseme flickering:

• 0.0: No smoothing (immediate response, may flicker)
• 0.3: Light smoothing (recommended balance)
• 0.7: Heavy smoothing (stable but slower response)
• 1.0: Maximum smoothing (very stable, delayed)

Reduces rapid switching between visemes for cleaner sequences.
Useful for noisy videos or subtle mouth movements.

enable_consonant_detection.label: Enable Consonant Detection
enable_consonant_detection.tooltip:
Detect consonants (B, P, M, F, V, TH, etc.) in addition to vowels:

• Vowels only: A, E, I, O, U, _
• With consonants: A, E, I, O, U, B, P, M, F, V, TH, _, etc.
• Adds ~10% processing time
• Provides more detailed phoneme sequences
• Better for advanced lip-sync and speech analysis

Leave disabled for basic vowel-only detection.

enable_temporal_analysis.label: Enable Temporal Analysis
enable_temporal_analysis.tooltip:
Advanced consonant burst detection using 5-frame windows:

• Analyzes onset → peak → release patterns for true consonants
• Dramatically improves B/P/M distinction accuracy
• Detects rapid lip closure/release vs sustained patterns
• Better coarticulation modeling (vowel context)
• Adds ~50% processing time but much higher accuracy
• Requires consonant detection enabled

Recommended for: research, high-quality phonetic analysis
Skip for: basic lip-sync, real-time processing

enable_word_prediction.label: Enable Word Prediction
enable_word_prediction.tooltip:
Predict words from detected phoneme sequences:

• Uses 10,000 most common English words
• Matches phoneme patterns to suggest likely words
• Shows confidence with ?, (), markers
• Example: 'AEIOU' → 'you', 'hey?', '(audio)'
• Helpful for manual SRT editing
• No processing time impact

Requires viseme detection enabled to work.

images.tooltip: Source video frames to slice.

num_slices.tooltip: Number of slices to divide the frame into

offset.tooltip: Frame offset step between slices. Negative reverses time.

angle.tooltip: Slice angle in degrees. 0 = vertical, 90 = horizontal, 45 = diagonal.

spacing.tooltip: How slice widths are distributed across the frame: even (linear), eased toward one side, or random.

direction.tooltip: Which slices carry the most time offset: building from one edge (forward/reverse), from the centre, or from both edges.

loop_mode.tooltip: How out-of-range frame indices are handled: wrap around (loop), bounce back (ping_pong), or shorten the clip (trim).

blend_width.tooltip: Soft blend width (px) across boundaries. 0 = hard edges.

seed.tooltip: Seed for 'random' spacing and slice jitter

cascade_curve.tooltip: How the per-slice offset grows across slices.

slice_jitter.tooltip: Random +/- frames added per slice (seeded). Adds glitchy irregularity.

animate.tooltip: Animate slices/offset/angle from start -> end over the clip.

num_slices_end.tooltip: Target slice count reached at the end of the animation.

offset_end.tooltip: Target per-slice frame offset at the end of the animation.

angle_end.tooltip: Target slice angle (degrees) at the end of the animation.

temporal_curve.tooltip: Easing applied to the start -> end animation over time.

frame_count.tooltip: Frames over which the animation completes. 0 = use clip length.

mask.tooltip: Optional mask. Slicing is applied only inside the white area; outside keeps the original frame.

TimeSliceEffect.name: TimeSliceEffect
TimeSliceEffect.description: Angled temporal slit-scan. Splits frames into slices offset in time, with cascade shaping and start->end animation.

images.tooltip: Source video frames to slice.

num_slices.tooltip: Number of slices to divide the frame into

max_offset.tooltip: Peak frame offset at the wave crest

wave_speed.tooltip: Full wave cycles over the clip. Higher = faster. Whole numbers loop seamlessly with loop_mode 'loop'.

wave_count.tooltip: Number of full sine cycles across all slices

angle.tooltip: Slice angle in degrees. 0 = vertical, 90 = horizontal.

loop_mode.tooltip: How out-of-range frame indices are handled: wrap around (loop), bounce back (ping_pong), or shorten the clip (trim).

blend_width.tooltip: Soft blend width (px) across boundaries. 0 = hard edges.

spacing.tooltip: How slice widths are distributed across the frame: even (linear), eased toward one side, or random.

seed.tooltip: Seed for 'random' spacing

mask.tooltip: Optional mask. Slicing is applied only inside the white area; outside keeps the original frame.

TimeSliceWave.name: TimeSliceWave
TimeSliceWave.description: Angled animated slit-scan with sinusoidal time displacement that ripples across the frame, creating an undulating temporal wave.

images_b.tooltip: Second source clip (B). Resized to match A if their dimensions differ.

num_slices.tooltip: Number of slices to divide the frame into

offset_a.tooltip: Frame offset step for A-source slices

offset_b.tooltip: Frame offset step for B-source slices

angle.tooltip: Slice angle in degrees. 0 = vertical, 90 = horizontal.

spacing.tooltip: How slice widths are distributed across the frame: even (linear), eased toward one side, or random.

direction.tooltip: Which slices carry the most time offset: building from one edge (forward/reverse), from the centre, or from both edges.

pattern.tooltip: How slices are assigned to the A and B clips across the frame.

loop_mode.tooltip: How out-of-range frame indices are handled: wrap around (loop), bounce back (ping_pong), or shorten the clip (trim).

blend_width.tooltip: Soft blend width (px) across boundaries. 0 = hard edges.

mix.tooltip: Balance between A and B. 0.5 = equal.

seed.tooltip: Seed for 'random' spacing, slice jitter and mix balancing

cascade_curve.tooltip: How the per-slice offset grows across slices.

TimeSliceDual.name: TimeSliceDual
TimeSliceDual.description: Dual-source angled slit-scan. Interleaves slices from two clips, each with its own time offset. Great for transitions and split-reality looks.

dtype.tooltip: Compute dtype. bfloat16 (default) matches UniVidX's training. float16 is functionally equivalent on most Blackwell/Ada cards. fp8_e4m3fn / fp8_e5m2 post-quantize the DiT via optimum-quanto's qfloat8 path: halves DiT memory (~28 GB → ~14 GB), enables Marlin FP8 matmul on Hopper/Blackwell. EXPERIMENTAL — the quantize() pass over Wan2.1-14B + UniVidX's LoRA stack is slow (10+ min) and may hang on some configurations; if your run stalls on cold-load, fall back to bfloat16.

compile_dit.tooltip: Run torch.compile(dit, mode='reduce-overhead', dynamic=True) after model load. First sampler step is 60-120 sec slower (graph capture), subsequent steps are typically 20-30% faster. Best for long runs at fixed resolution; loses its compile cache when you change resolution/frame-count. Cached separately per (variant, dtype, compile) tuple so toggling triggers a re-load + re-compile.

prefer_sage_attn.tooltip: If True (and `sageattention` is installed in the ComfyUI venv), monkey-patch DiffSynth's Wan DiT attention chain so SageAttention wins over Flash Attention 2. SageAttention's INT8-quantized attention is typically faster on Hopper/Blackwell (claimed 2-5x by upstream, our measurements vary). On Blackwell (sm_120) FA3 isn't available — FA2 is the default winner — so this flag is the main attention-backend lever. No-op if sageattention isn't installed.

vram_buffer_gb.tooltip: GB of VRAM kept free for activations / KV cache / VAE decode. Passed to UniVidX's pipeline-level enable_vram_management(), which wraps text encoder + DiT + VAE through DiffSynth's offload helper so layers live on CPU and stream to GPU on demand. Higher = more headroom but more streaming (slower). Lower = more residency. 4.0 GB is a sane default for BF16 Wan2.1-14B + UniVidX LoRAs on 32 GB cards. Cached per (variant, dtype, vram_buffer, ...) so two loader nodes with different values get distinct model instances.

offload_strategy.tooltip: Memory strategy for the Wan2.1 DiT. `balanced` uses vram_buffer_gb to keep part of the DiT resident on GPU. `auto` is balanced plus a 24GB safety clamp. `layered_cpu_offload` keeps DiT layers on CPU and copies each layer to GPU only for its forward pass. It is slower but the safest option for 24GB cards, especially with step_distill_lora enabled.

step_distill_lora.tooltip: Merge a step-distillation LoRA into the DiT base weights at load time, enabling near-production-quality decompositions at 4-6 sample steps + cfg_scale=1. Cuts wall-time per chunk by ~3-5x. Currently supports 'lightx2v' (Wan2.1-T2V-14B-StepDistill-CfgDistill-Lightx2v, rank-32). EXPERIMENTAL: step-distill quality on UniVidX's per-modality decompositions (Albedo / Irradiance / Normal / Alpha) is unverified - LightX2V was trained on natural-image content, not on synthetic decomposition targets. RGB-style outputs are most likely to retain quality; Normal and Alpha mattes are highest risk. Pairs with `step_distill_strength`. Requires the file under models/loras/lightx2v/ (see FileNotFoundError message for download cmd).

step_distill_strength.tooltip: Effective merge strength for the step-distill LoRA. 1.0 = standard merge (recommended for the distillation effect); 0.0 = no merge (equivalent to step_distill_lora='none'); >1.0 = overdrive (may produce artifacts but worth testing if 1.0 gives weak step-reduction effect on your content). Cached as part of the model key, so changing this triggers a full reload.

dit_weight_mode.tooltip:
How the DiT weights are stored after load. 0.5.0 default: `fp8_prequantized`. 

`fp8_prequantized` (recommended): the DiT's ~400 Linears + biases + norms are converted to FP8 e4m3fn after the standard BF16 cold-load. Two implementation paths share this label — (a) FILE-BASED if a Kijai `Wan2_1-T2V-14B_fp8_e4m3fn_scaled.safetensors` is present under models/diffusion_models/ (no such file exists upstream for Wan2.1 as of 0.5.0; reserved forward-compat slot), (b) RUNTIME-QUANTIZE otherwise (the actual 0.5.0 path on every Wan2.1 install today). Quality: PSNR ≥ 30 dB per modality vs BF16 reference. Wall: 9.43 min on R2AIN_video, 13% faster than bf16_shards, ~14 GB DiT VRAM. 

`bf16_shards`: standard BF16 path — ~28 GB DiT in VRAM (with vram_buffer streaming layers as needed). The 0.3.x baseline. Pixel-for-pixel identical to UniVidX's vanilla output but slower. 

`auto` (legacy): preserved for back-compat with old saved workflows. In 0.5.0+ this resolves to `fp8_prequantized` (was `bf16_shards` in 0.4.0). 

`fp8_runtime_experimental`: legacy mmgp.offload.quantize() pass after BF16 cold load — known to hang on this stack. Kept only as an escape hatch for users who need to replicate pre-0.4.0 quirks; will be removed in 0.6.0.

num_inference_steps.tooltip: Number of denoising steps. UniVidX is trained at 20 (production preset). With step_distill_lora=lightx2v on the loader + cfg_scale=1.0, use 4 (the fast-preview preset, ~5x faster wall, ~22-26 dB PSNR vs production reference). 50+ rarely helps and usually hurts on this model.

AdvancedCalculator.name: AdvancedCalculator
AdvancedCalculator.description:
Advanced Calculator (Expression-based)
    VARIABLES (case-insensitive):
      A, B, C, D, E
      - Optional inputs
      - Unconnected inputs default to 0
      - Accepts INT / FLOAT / STRING (auto-cast)
    --------------------------------------------------
    EXPRESSION RULES:
      - Multiline expressions supported
      - Newlines and extra whitespace are removed automatically
      - Variables and function names are case-insensitive
    --------------------------------------------------
    AVAILABLE FUNCTIONS:
      Basic Math:
        ceil(x)     : round up
        floor(x)    : round down
        round(x)    : round to nearest
        abs(x)      : absolute value
      Min / Max:
        min(a, b, ...)
        max(a, b, ...)
      Power / Roots:
        pow(a, b)   : a raised to power b
        sqrt(x)     : square root
      Fractional:
        frac(x)     : fractional part of x
                      defined as x - floor(x)
                      works correctly for negatives
    --------------------------------------------------
    ERROR HANDLING:
      - Invalid expressions return 0
      - Unconnected inputs are treated as 0
      - Safe evaluation (no system or file access)

anchor_mode.tooltip:
How the exposure reference is chosen.
middle: use a window around anchor_center as the reference (recommended for WAN drift at BOTH start/end).
tail: use the last ref_tail_frames as the reference (useful when the end is known-stable).

ref_tail_frames.tooltip:
Only used when anchor_mode=tail.
Number of final frames sampled to compute the reference exposure (median log-luma).
Increase if the tail is stable but noisy; decrease if the tail contains fades/changes.

anchor_center.tooltip:
Only used when anchor_mode=middle.
Normalized position (0..1) for the center of the anchor window.
0.50 anchors the middle; 0.55 biases slightly later if the beginning is more unstable.

anchor_window.tooltip:
Only used when anchor_mode=middle.
Number of frames in the anchor window used to compute the reference exposure.
Larger is more robust, but avoid spanning major scene changes.

correct_ends.tooltip:
Which regions to correct.
start_only: correct only the initial transient until it settles.
start_and_end: also correct tail drift if the last stable_count frames are outside tolerance_ev.

tolerance_ev.tooltip:
Stability tolerance in exposure stops (EV).
Lower = stricter (detects drift longer, may correct more frames).
Higher = more forgiving (corrects fewer frames, less risk of reacting to content changes).

stable_count.tooltip:
How many consecutive frames must be within tolerance_ev to be considered stable.
Higher values reduce false-stability on noisy sequences but may delay settle detection.

max_correct_frames.tooltip:
Hard cap on how many frames can be corrected at the start and (if enabled) at the end.
0 disables correction entirely (stats/report only).

proxy_size.tooltip:
Downscale size used to compute luminance statistics.
0 uses full resolution (slower). 64–128 is usually sufficient and much faster.

gain_min.tooltip:
Minimum allowed exposure gain applied to any frame.
Lower values allow stronger darkening correction but can crush highlights if too low.

gain_max.tooltip:
Maximum allowed exposure gain applied to any frame.
Higher values allow stronger brightening correction but can clip highlights if too high.

gain_smooth_window.tooltip:
Temporal smoothing window for the per-frame gain curve.
Use odd values. Larger values reduce pumping but can lag real drift.
The anchor window is forced to gain=1.0 after smoothing.

clip_low.tooltip:
Luminance clamp floor used ONLY for computing stats (not applied to output pixels).
Raise slightly (e.g., 0.02–0.05) to reduce influence of deep blacks/noise on exposure estimation.

clip_high.tooltip:
Luminance clamp ceiling used ONLY for computing stats (not applied to output pixels).
Lower slightly (e.g., 0.98–0.995) to reduce influence of specular peaks on exposure estimation.

XB_ComicPromptParser.display_name: XB-BOX - 📝 漫画提示词智能解析
XB_ComicPromptParser.description:
前端提示词拦截解析器 —— SSOT 架构核心。
输入含 [台词] 的完整剧本，自动:
1. 提取 [] 内台词，拼接为台词1|台词2 格式
2. 根据字数映射气泡尺寸 (<=3:微小, <=8:标准, <=18:宽大, >18:超大)
3. 清洗提示词，彻底屏蔽大模型看到汉字，根除鬼影

XB_AutoBubbleTextRenderer.name: XB_AutoBubbleTextRenderer
XB_AutoBubbleTextRenderer.display_name: XB-BOX - 🤖 漫画文字渲染 (全自动带涂改液)
XB_AutoBubbleTextRenderer.description:
第二代全自动 CV 视觉锚定节点 (v3.0 生产版)。

流程: 灰度化 -> 形态学闭运算填平噪点 -> 二值化 -> 轮廓检测 -> 涂改液抹白 -> 填字。

核心能力:
- auto_clear_bubble: 数字涂改液，先抹后写彻底根除鬼影
- morph_close_size: 形态学预处理，解决气泡内纹理/残影导致的识别断裂
- 三层防御: 暗黑模式(invert) + 形状过滤(shape_filter) + 边界分离(erode)
- 台词框输入 台词1 | 台词2 | 台词3，一键自动排版

| name | description |

LoraTagPowerLoader.name: LoraTagPowerLoader
LoraTagPowerLoader.description:
Power LoRA loader that detects LoRA tags in text input.
Supports dual noise weighting for WanVideo/Hunyuan models.

Tag Format:
- <lora:name:weight> - Sets model weight for both high/low noise. CLIP uses default_weight.
- <lora:name:high:low> - Different model weights for high/low noise passes. CLIP uses default_weight.
- <lora:name:high:low:clip> - Full control: separate high/low model weights and explicit CLIP weight.

Features:
- Text-based tag detection (like ImpactWildcardEncode)
- Unlimited LoRA loading (like Power Lora Loader)
- Dual noise weight support (high/low noise passes)
- WanVideo/Hunyuan compatibility with video_model_mode
- LoRA caching for performance
- Global weight multiplier for quick adjustments

Noise Mode:
- high_noise: Use high noise weights (for early generation passes)
- low_noise: Use low noise weights (for detail refinement passes)
- auto: Average of high and low weights

For WanVideo/Hunyuan dual LoRA loading, use two instances of this node with different noise_mode settings.

images.tooltip: Your clip (frames×H×W×C).

offset.tooltip: How far to rotate the clip. Positive = forward in time; negative = backward.

images.tooltip: Clip after interpolation (frames′×H×W×C).

base_offset.tooltip: Use the exact offset_out that came from RollFrames.

m.tooltip: How many in-betweens per gap were added (the interpolation multiple).

UnrollFrames.description: Undo a previous roll after interpolation by accounting for the inserted frames (rotate by base_offset × (m+1)).

clip_frames.tooltip: Your full clip (NHWC, 0–1). Tries every crop from 0..max_end_crop_frames and returns the best loop.

max_end_crop_frames.tooltip: Largest crop to test at the END. Higher = more candidates (slower), but potentially better.

include_first_step.tooltip: Use the first neighbor pair (frame 0→1) as a target step size/similarity.

include_last_step.tooltip: Use the last neighbor pair inside the KEPT region as a target.

include_global_median_step.tooltip: Also use the median step across the KEPT region (needs ≥3 frames). Helps ignore outliers.

seam_window_frames.tooltip: Average over multiple aligned pairs across the seam. Larger = more robust.

distance_metric.tooltip: How to measure step size for matching. L1 is usually more forgiving; MSE penalizes big errors more.

score_in_8bit.tooltip: Score with an 8-bit view (simulate export). Output video still stays float.

use_ssim_similarity.tooltip: Include SSIM so the seam ‘looks’ like a normal neighbor—avoid freeze or jump.

use_exposure_guard.tooltip: Promote smooth brightness across the seam (reduces flicker pops).

use_flow_guard.tooltip: Encourage consistent motion across the seam (needs OpenCV; slower).

weight_step_size.tooltip: Importance of matching step size. Higher = less freeze/jump risk.

weight_similarity.tooltip: Importance of visual similarity (SSIM). Helps avoid a frozen-looking seam.

weight_exposure.tooltip: Importance of even brightness across the seam.

weight_flow.tooltip: Importance of motion continuity across the seam.

ssim_downsample_scales.tooltip: SSIM scales to average, as a comma list. Example: 1,2 = full-res and half-res.

accelerate_with_gpu.tooltip: If ON and CUDA is available, run scoring on GPU for a big speedup (same results).

use_mixed_precision.tooltip: If ON (with GPU), use mixed precision for SSIM/conv math (faster on larger clips).

AutocropToLoop.name: AutocropToLoop
AutocropToLoop.description: Auto-crops the clip to create a smoother loop: tests crops from the end and scores the seam so it feels like a normal step.

UpscaleWithModelAdvanced.name: UpscaleWithModelAdvanced
UpscaleWithModelAdvanced.description:
Based on Comfy's native "Upscale Image (using Model)", with controls exposed to tune for large batches, avoid slow
OOM fallbacks, and create opportunities to optimize for speed.

Defaults
- Behaves about the same as the original node.

Controls
- max_batch_size > 0: process images in chunks to keep VRAM steady and reduce fallback slowdowns.
- tile_size: choose a starting tile; original node defaults to 512. 0 = auto (falls back 512 → 256 → 128 on OOM).
- channels_last: try ON for a speedup on some systems.
- precision: lower (fp16/bf16) can be faster; may impact quality depending on the model.

• Crop: final output width

height.tooltip:

Notes:
• Keep AR / Pad: maximum height for the fit
• Crop: final output height
• AR Scale + Divisible Crop: requested height before divisibility

resize_mode.tooltip:
Modes:
- Keep AR: Fit inside width×height (preserve aspect)
- Stretch: Force to width×height (may distort)
- Crop (Cover + Crop): Scale to cover, then crop to width×height
- Pad (Fit + Pad): Fit inside, then pad to width×height
- AR Scale + Divisible Crop: Scale by SOURCE long side to ≤ requested divisible; crop ONLY the short side to its divisible

divisible_by.tooltip:
Force output dimensions to multiples of N.

Details:
• Keep AR: Fit → then step down to the largest size ≤ requested that keeps AR AND makes both sides divisible
• AR Scale + Divisible Crop: Lock the scaled LONG side to its divisible target; crop ONLY the short side to its divisible
Set to 1 (or 0 in UI) to disable

max_batch_size.tooltip:
0 = process whole batch
>0 = chunk the batch to this size

sinc_window.tooltip: Lanczos window size (a). Higher = sharper (more ringing).

pad_color.tooltip: Pad mode only. RGB as 'r, g, b' (0-255).

Choose which edges are preserved for cropping, or where padding is added.

precision.tooltip: Resampling compute dtype.

LoadVideoFromUrl.name: LoadVideoFromUrl
LoadVideoFromUrl.description:
Load Video (Path) 🎥🅥🅗🅢
Loads a video from an arbitrary path
[-]
Inputs:
[-]
meta_batch: (optional) Connect to a Meta Batch manager to divide extremely long sequences into sub batches. See the documentation for Meta Batch Manager
[-]
vae: (optional) If provided the node will output latents instead of images. This drastically reduces the required RAM (not VRAM) when working with long (100+ frames) sequences
Using this is strongly encouraged unless connecting to a node that requires a blue image connection such as Apply Controllnet
[-]
Outputs:
[-]
IMAGE: The loaded images
[-]
frame_count: The length of images just returned
[-]
audio: The audio from the loaded video
[-]
video_info: Exposes additional info about the video such as the source frame rate, or the total length
[-]
LATENT: The loaded images pre-converted to latents. Only available when a vae is connected
[-]
Widgets:
[-]
video: The video file to be loaded.
You can also select an image to load it as a single frame
This is a VHS_PATH input. When edited, it provides a list of possible valid files or directories
The current top-most completion may be selected with Tab
You can navigate up a directory by pressing Ctrl+B (or Ctrl+W if supported by browser)
The filter on suggested file types can be disabled by pressing Ctrl+G.
If converted to an input, this functions as a string
[-]
force_rate: Drops or duplicates frames so that the produced output has the target frame rate. Many motion models are trained on videos of a specific frame rate and will give better results if input matches that frame rate. If set to 0, all frames are returned. May give unusual results with inputs that have a variable frame rate like animated gifs. Reducing this value can also greatly reduce the execution time and memory requirements.
[-]
force_size: Previously was used to provide suggested resolutions. Instead, custom_width and custom_height can be disabled by setting to 0.
[-]
custom_width: Allows for an arbitrary width to be entered, cropping to maintain aspect ratio if both are set
[-]
custom_height: Allows for an arbitrary height to be entered, cropping to maintain aspect ratio if both are set
[-]
frame_load_cap: The maximum number of frames to load. If 0, all frames are loaded.
[-]
skip_first_frames: A number of frames which are discarded before producing output.
[-]
select_every_nth: Similar to frame rate. Keeps only the first of every n frames and discard the rest. Has better compatibility with variable frame rate inputs such as gifs. When combined with force_rate, select_every_nth_applies after force_rate so the resulting output has a frame rate equivalent to force_rate/select_every_nth. select_every_nth does not apply to skip_first_frames
[-]
format: Updates other widgets so that only values supported by the given format can be entered and provides recommended defaults.
[-]
videopreview: Displays a preview for the selected video input. Will only be shown if Advanced Previews is enabled. This preview will reflect the frame_load_cap, force_rate, skip_first_frames, and select_every_nth values chosen. If the video has audio, it will also be previewed when moused over. Additional preview options can be accessed with right click.

threshold.tooltip: 灵敏度。算法基于颜色直方图状态变化（对人物运动/镜头运动鲁棒），threshold 控制检测严格度：0.05=较敏感（弱变化也抓），0.08=默认（平衡），0.12=保守（只抓明显变化）。不同视频无需逐条调参。

max_resolution.tooltip: 缩放后最长边的目标像素数。0 = 不缩放（用原始分辨率，内存占用大）。默认 512 足够保留分镜检测细节，同时大幅节省内存。

frame_rate.tooltip: 输出帧率（fps）。卡点位置会按此帧率转换为帧数。常见：24、25、30、60。

mode.tooltip: 踩节拍1：密集节拍检测（剪映风格），可用 beat_count 指定数量。强变化点：只检测 drop / 副歌进入，忽略 beat_count。

beat_count.tooltip: 期望卡点数。0=自动检测所有节拍；>0=在所有候选节拍中均匀选 N 个（必须满足在节拍上的前提下）。仅在踩节拍1模式下生效。

sensitivity.tooltip: 灵敏度。0=检测较多变化点，1=只检测最强 drop/beat。踩节拍1模式默认 0.2；强变化点模式建议调到 0.3-0.5。

min_segment_frames.tooltip: 最短段帧数。短于此值的段会被合并到相邻段。踩节拍1默认 12 (0.5s @ 24fps)；强变化点建议调到 36+。

AI autoprompter for Ideogram 4's structured JSON caption format.

Describe an idea (and/or drop a reference image) in the node UI and let a local
vision LLM (Qwen3-VL, default) or Gemini build the full caption — background,

assembled caption JSON string (plus a preview).

padding_percent.tooltip: Expands the detected region before rectangle fitting.
